sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: Synthesis over enumeration. Instead of listing placements, name the two or three patterns the chart keeps producing. A through-line is only real when the chart says it more than one way; a single placement is a detail, not a pattern.

sections.heading: Philosophy
sections.body: Anchored to the house stance (see stance_chart_story.json): the chart speaks clearly about the shape of the story, less clearly about the choices made within it, least clearly about the exact scenes. Name the shape; hold the choices open; never predict the scene.

sections.heading: Factor Weights
sections.body: Proposed, tunable. Mirrors the transit_significance scoring idea, applied to the natal chart to find what carries the most weight.

items.label: dignityModifier
items.body: multiply a factor up for domicile/exaltation, down for detriment/fall.

sections.heading: Repetition Rule
sections.body: A through-line must be echoed by at least two independent signatures (for example a sign emphasis AND a house emphasis AND/OR an aspect). This is the guardrail against over-reading one placement, the same logic as 'a synastry bond needs multiple indicators' and the generational-vs-personal stellium check.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Use this order to turn many natal factors into two or three through-lines.

items.label: Step 1
items.body: Score every chart factor for emphasis using the weights above.

items.label: Step 2
items.body: Group the high-weight factors by shared theme (element, principle, life-area, or keyword).

items.label: Step 3
items.body: Keep only themes the chart states two or more ways; these are the through-lines.

items.label: Step 4
items.body: Name each plainly, in the second person, as a tendency.

items.label: Step 5
items.body: Pair each with its choice point so it reads as a pattern you can work with, not a verdict.

sections.heading: Output Shape
sections.body: Through-lines: 2 to 3 maximum. Each through-line should include a name, what it is, evidence, and a choice point.

items.label: name
items.body: a plain-language pattern, e.g. 'you keep depth and distance in the same hand'

items.label: whatItIs
items.body: the felt tendency in one or two sentences

items.label: evidence
items.body: the placements that say it (the repetition that makes it real)

items.label: choicePoint
items.body: the agency: what is learned and changeable here, and the decision it leaves you

sections.heading: Honesty Rules
sections.body: Keep natal synthesis descriptive and agency-forward.

items.label: shape_clear
items.body: State the pattern with confidence; this is what a chart can show.

items.label: choices_held_open
items.body: Always frame as a tendency plus a choice, never a fixed outcome.

items.label: scenes_not_predicted
items.body: Never name specific future events; the chart does not speak clearly there.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Use these as pattern examples, not fixed scripts.

items.label: Example 1
items.body: Depth through-line: a Scorpio Sun, an 8th-house stellium, and Moon square Pluto all say the same thing three ways. You go deep and don't do surface; intimacy is high-stakes. The shape is real; the choice is whether depth becomes connection or control.

items.label: Example 2
items.body: Freedom-versus-security through-line: Moon in Cancer (needs roots) opposed by Uranus (needs escape), with Aquarius rising. You're pulled between belonging and breaking free. The tension is built in; the work is holding both, not picking one.

items.label: Example 3
items.body: Visibility through-line: Sun conjunct the Midheaven, a Leo emphasis, and a 10th-house stellium. You're built to be seen and to lead. The drive is real; the choice is whether you lead for recognition or for the work.

sections.heading: Integration
sections.body: Pulls evidence from planet_in_sign, planet_in_house, the aspect corpora, stelliums, chiron, nodal, and lilith; scores with the transit_significance approach; frames with stance_chart_story. It is the layer that turns the data into two or three things worth saying.
